findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250  Observed the prep cooler by the 2-door Coke cooler to be holding temperature at 54F. Noodles within the cooler were probed at 55F. Noodles were discarded during the inspection. Cooler was not turned to coldest setting during the inspection. Other foods present in the cooler included prepped raw vegetables (broccoli and onions) and personal foods. Sliced tomatoes were on a fresh flat and moved to the walk-in cooler. 2) Mini-cooler across from the woks is observed keeping temperature at 65F. Foods inside included produce, shrimp, and lobster. Discarded during the inspection. 3) Raw chicken  and fried wontons are observed on a counter adjacent to the water heater. Foods are observed at 57F. Discarded during inspection. 4) Fried shrimp is observed resting on a counter across from the sushi preparation table. Observed at temperature of 67F. Discarded during the inspection. 5) Reconstituted noodles are observed in a bucket at room temperature across from the woks. Moved to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service. Staff indicated rice was allowed to set on racks to cool just around 1:45. Rice is allowed to be kept.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-250 Soup of the day is observed held on top of the steam table at 119F. Soup of the day is only served at lunch. Kitchen was closed between lunch and dinner. It is a poor practice to leave food uncovered and out of temperature even if it will be discarded before dinner. Discarded during inspection. Discard foods between services. Also, milk-base sauce is observed also sitting on top of the steam table at 81F. Milk product was discarded during the inspection. Cease allowing foods to rest on counters between service periods. This is an incredibly poor food handling strategy and should cease immediately.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135°F or above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed three deep tubs of cooling rice being stored adajcent to the electrical panels in the back room (across from walk-in coolers). Tubs of cooked rice were probed and found 130F-108F, 113F - 96F, and 126F - 103F throughout the three pans. Items were placed in the freezer to speed cooling process and then moved to the walk-in cooler. Manager on duty was not aware of when rice was cooked and left to cool. He was instructed to ask the cooks when the rice was placed on the cooling racks. Any time before noon and the rice is to be discarded. Cooked rice was also observed in a covered bowl on a counter by the hot water heater. This rice observed at 57F. This bowl was discarded during the inspection.  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed a tub of a dozen portions of salmon and other frozen fish thawing underneath the counter of the sushi kitchen. Food was moved to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. Cease thawing foods at room temperature. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  The poor practice of leaving food-covered utensils on counters in-between shifts is observed. Observed knives on magnetic knife strips over three compartment sink to be soiled from prior use. The metal knife caddies with hibachi chef blades are observed thickly coated with food (both knives and interior of metal sheaths), and whisks with flour, broth, and milk base are observed stored in various containers of same product. At room temperature within and around the produce preparation cooler by the woks. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. 750-130(d) Observed shrimp stored under beef and chicken in the walk-in cooler. Most of the product was moved during the inspection. Store foods in their proper cooking order.  All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Foods throughout the facility are observed uncovered and exposed to possible overhead contamination and frost. Observed the following uncovered foods: 1) raw chicken and fried wontons on a counter next to the hot water heater; 2) three tubs of bread crumbs stored on-top of the single door Coke cooler; 3) ice cream at the wait station reach-in cooler; 4) soup, noodles, and milk base across from the woks on the cookline; and 5) soda station ice bin. Cover foods in-between busy periods to protect from possible overhead contamination. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 Dipper well in the wait station is not functioning. Ice cream scoops are observed stored in milky/frothy water. Pulled from use during the inspection. Observed knives stored inbetween the prep cooler and the counter across from the woks. Cease storing knives inbetween surfaces that cannot be cleaned. Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells. Magnetic, wall-mounted knife strips throughout the kitchen are observed soiled. Whisks, strainers, and other food handling scoops are observed being stored on soiled surfaces and with food still attached. Kitchen is closed between lunch and dinner. All in-use utensils should be removed to the dish machine for proper cleaning.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed personal drinks on top of coolers and food in various places throughout the facility. Open glasses of water were observed over clean equipment in the wait area, on top of the prep cooler by the 2-door Coke cooler and over the preparation counter across from the woks. An opened bottle of water is observed on the top shelf of the 2-door Coke cooler. Moved all personal beverages during the inspection.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a Ice cream scoops in the wait area are observed pitted from repeat use and with damaged handles. Cease use of pitted scoops. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-600  Observed cardboard and cloths around the kitchen to act as grease absorption and to stop equipment from moving. REMOVE CARDBOARD FROM FACILITY. Cardboard is observed lining the counters of the island preparation tables. Cloths are observed on roll carts and under cutting boards. Cease use of absorbent materials. Cardboard is a possible source of your pest problem as roaches and eggs travel in the corrugated grooves of the cardboard. Reach-in freezer on the cookline and the ice cream freezer in the wait area are observed coated with frost. In addition to these two reach-ins, the walk-in freezer has cascading frost along the door side wall. It appears that the door was not properly closed during an overnight or extended period of time. Food appears sound, just coated with frost.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable
MAINTENANCE: The left side of the wait station counter (to the right of the soda machine) has a section of stainless steel pulling from remaining counter. There are roaches observed crawling in this gap. Seal the section of pulled stainless to the counter. Eliminate gaps and potential housing for pests.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-830f Soiled dishes are being left on roll carts in the dish area and the wait area inbetween lunch and dinner service. Cease this practice. Maintain kitchen clean and free from food and water sources between lunch and dinner service and overnight. Drainboards and three compartment sinks are observed soiled with gross food debris and grease. Clean the sinks and the drainboards.  Equipment and utensils shall be placed into the dish machine in a way that food-contact surfaces are exposed to the unobstructed application of detergents, wash, and clean rinse water, and that permits free draining.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800d Too many surfaces to list, however, cleaning practices were discussed with manager. There is obvious general cleaning occurring at the facility, it is the detail cleaning that is not frequently and properly being conducted. Steamer, cookers, fryers, ovens, and refrigerators are observed with food splash and grease along the edges and interior of the units. Knife caddies and utensils containers on roll carts for hibachi grill and on the cookline are observed soiled with accumulated food. Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e See violation #23 as well. There are too many surfaces to produce a proper laundry list. The manager was able to accompany inspector through kitchen and see various surfaces needing cleaning attention. The kitchen has not cleaned along the roll carts, handles of equipment, shelving, sides of counters, garbage cans, underside of sink basins and counters, and along sides of all equipment. There is a thick accumulation of food and grease around every piece of equipment. Cleaning was discussed with staff. Deep cleaning was began during the inspection. It is suggested that a methodical approach be taken to cleaning this kitchen: start from ceiling to floor and clean clockwise around the kitchen. Pay attention to the lips and grooves of sinks and counters. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Cleaned dishes are observed being stored on soiled roll carts adajcent to the dish machine. Clean the roll carts and store them in a manner that will protect them from splash. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) Bucket of waste water observed under the 3-part sink by the dish machine. Water was old and coated with a layer of film and molds. Bucket was picked-up to be discarded and roaches were observed underneath. Discarded during inspection. There was also old mop water observed in the mop bucket. Discarded during the inspection. There is an obvious roach concern in this facility. Cease allowing liquids and foods to accumulate in the kitchen. You are providing a food and water source for pests.  Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 There is a leak at the three compartment sink adjacent to the dishmachine. See violation #28 also. Repair this leak and properly deal with the waste water in the interim. Waste water should be drained daily and the catch basin should be cleaned. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 There is an on-going roach concern in this kitchen. An active population of all llife stages is observed throughout the facility. Roaches were observed at the dish machine and the three compartment sink to the right of the machine. Roaches were observed crawling underneath the 2-door Coke cooler and the adajcent prep cooler and mop sink. Roaches are observed crawling across the top of the island preparation counters across from the woks. Roaches are observed crawling around the water heater to the left of the woks. The pests were observed around the garbage cans and the prep coolers at the sushi bar in front of the kitchen. Finally, roaches are observed around the reach-in ice cream cooler and the soda machine of the wait area.  Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control. DRAIN FLIES are observed at the soiled linen bag by the mop sink. Dozens of the flies were observed when the bag was kicked.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Floors throughout are being cleaned. Detail cleaning is not occurring. There is a thick, black grease and food accumulation around the wall-to-floor areas and around the legs and wheels of equipment. This is observed throughout the entire facility. Pay attention to scrubbing between large equipment and small crevices. The floor in the wait area between the soda station and the adjacent counters is observed thickly coated with soil, gross food accumulation, water, and molds. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 Grout around the mop sink is low. This is allowing for ponding water and for roaches to easily travel from cooler to mop sink. Refill grout around the mop sink.  All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
Floors drains are observed thickly coated with mold and soil. Clean the floor drains.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Walls throughout are observed clean. The wall around the three compartment sink by the swing doors is observed soiled with splash as is the dish machine area. Drainlines from all sinks are observed soiled with accumulated molds and soil. Plumbing beneath the three compartment sink by the dish machine is observed crawling with roaches. The grease along the plumbing lines from the back of the dish machine are again observed thickly coated with grease. Roaches were observed crawling along these plumbing lines.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Employee coat is observed stored on the rolling can rack in the back room. Aprons for the hibachi grill area are observed being stored on the food of the rolling carts. Aprons were observed on top of eggs and utensils resting prepared for dinner service. Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed lemon juice stored on a shelf over a drainboard of the 3-part sink mixed in with sanitizer tablets, roach killer, and soap. Moved during inspection. Observed eye drops stored within the hinged lid of the top of the prep cooler adjacent to the 2-door Coke cooler. Also, observed anti-septic bandage spray on top of carrots in the mini-cooler across from the woks. All items were moved during the inspection. Cease stored chemicals in areas of food storage and preparation. All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
750-1160 Facility is not conducting a cleaning and maintenance schedule that will prohibit the harboring of pests. Water and food sources are abundant. Possible housing is being supplied through cardboard and general lack of maintenance and cleaning. The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.
750-1390 Observed a mop resting within old mop water in the mop bucket. Cease allowing mop water to rest between lunch and dinner. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-1380a Soiled linens are observed resting on the two island counters on the left side of the kitchen. The linen bag in front of the mop sink has not been properly maintained and is providing a breeding ground for pests.  Clean clothes and linens shall be stored in a clean place and protected from contamination until used.  Properly store all linens.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Observed the rice spatula from the previous evening's service still stored in water. Emptied during the inspection. See violation #22 as well. Make sure that all potential food sources and potential sources of cross-contamination are removed for cleaning nightly. The water in the rice utensil storage container should be changed every four hours and discarded nightly. Cease leaving utensils in water overnight. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-830i Observed dishes from the previous evening's service stacked on two rolling carts in front of the dish machine. Utensils, equipment, glassware are from Thursday night service. The presence of food on these dishes serves as a potential food and water source for pests. Cease this activity. Do not allow so many dishes to rest overnight. Send all soiled equipment through the dish machine and make sure that the machine is washed. All dishwashing machines shall be thoroughly cleaned at least once a day or more often when necessary to maintain them in satisfactory operating condition. 750-830f Equipment and utensils shall be placed into the dish machine in a way that food-contact surfaces are exposed to the unobstructed application of detergents, wash, and clean rinse water, and that permits free draining.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800d Observed the dish machine to be soiled with accumulated food crumbs, soil, and mineral deposits from use without proper cleaning. Dish machine was observed at start of the day with no dish service started. During the inspection, observed the first wash load being run. Cease allowing gross food debris to rest on machine overnight. You have a known infestation at this location. Clean the dish machine. Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 There is still an active roach population present at this facility. Observed all stages of active life moving around the dishmachine. The facility is not cleaning thoroughly and is not insuring that dishes, food sources, and water sources are removed nightly. A serious detail cleaning should be conducted with continued spot treatment from your pest control specialist. The amount of food debris, water, and soil available for pests is not going to allow for effective pest control treament. You must clean and operate responsibly to insure pests cease activity.  Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 The floor around the dishmachine is observed soiled with accumulated grease, food, and soil. Clean and scrub the floors and coving as necessary to maintain them clean.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 The plumbing and walls around the dishmachine are observed soiled with grease and food debris. Clean the walls. The ATTACHED PLUMBING RUNNING UP THE WALL from the dish machine has serious grease accumulation. Roaches are observed running along this black, greased plumbing into the ceiling. Clean the area surrounding the dish machine to eliminate food and soil.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b The walk-in cooler is observed holding foods at temperatures around 34-36F. Observed wrapped bags of noodles and bulk tubs of rice to be cooling and not have the time or date indicated. The rice was made last night. Discussed the need to indicate the time the food is placed in the walk-in cooler for cooling and the need to use a stem thermometer for monitoring time/temperature. The last guy out should be using his stem thermometer to make sure that the rice is properly cooler and that benchmarks have been met (hot temp to 70F within two hours and from 70-41F within four hours). Put someone in charge of checking on the cooling foods. There were approximately one dozen bulk brown tubs of cooling rice and another dozen bags of cooling noodles. The potential to improperly cool is great. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed a bulk box and several bags of shrimp thawing on the drainboard of the 3-part sink. Employee was asked to properly thaw shrimp under cold running water during the inspection. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed several carts holding clean bowls and serving pieces across from the dish machine. The carts themselves are observed significantly soiled (see violation #24). The small plates and bowls being stored at this location are coated with splash from the preparation line. Plates are covered with old rice and bowls are observed holding slices vegetables. During the inspection, the clean equipment was pulled for cleaning. Watch the storage of clean equipment so that food does not fall onto the clean surface and lead to cross-contamination. These pieces of equipment are not being stored in direct contact with a food preparation location and should not be so soiled with bulk food.  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a)  Observed breadcrumbs, sauces, and wok prep cart to have foods not covered overnight. Also, observed all the cooling foods to be either covered or tightly bagged. Watch that foods are properly handled as they go through the various stages of service in the kitchen. Foods being cooled should be left uncovered. Foods left at room temperature overnight should be covered with plastic wrap/parchment paper/lids. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed one employee enter the back door, don his apron, and immediately begin working with food. Another employee switched tasks from handling soiled roll cart to handling clean dishes. Yet another employee was observed entering the kitchen and going directly into food preparation. Discussed handwashing with staff and managers. Wash hands everytime you switch tasks and especially inbetween touching raw foods or soiled equipment and food preparation. Staff should come into work and immediately wash hands. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed personal opened bottled water on the top shelf of the 2-door Coke cooler and a glass cup over the adjacent preparation cooler. Cease storing personal drinks over food and equipment. Store beverages low and away so if they spill no other food or equipment is contaminated. Should you wish to keep a personal beverage at your work station the cup should be disposable with a lid and a straw. Moved personal drinks during the inspection. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 The dish machine is not properly sanitizing dishes. GFS was contacted last week and the machine needed a part ordered. GFS anticipates ten business days to receive the part. During the inspection, dishes were being run through the dish machine, however, no third sink was being used for sanitizing. The dish operator was able to immediately set-up a sink for sanitizing dishes. Discussed using the dish machine for the washing and rinsing process and then dipping the trays of dishes into the sink for 60 seconds to allow for sanitizing. This process is tedious and is not a viable substitute for a functioning dish machine. Make sure that this step is followed through the busy weekend. All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

Preparation work has begun in the kitchen and one of the necessary tools is a sani-bucket for in-use wiping cloths. Use a bleach cloth to wipe down counters. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800d Observed rice from yesterday's service to be stuck along the edges of the rice steamers. Also, the drainboards of the dishmachine and 3-part sinks are observed coated with gross food debris and grease. Discussed cleaning of these surfaces immediately with manager and staff. Sinks were wiped as were drainboards. Keep food contact surfaces clean in an effort to prevent cross contamination.  Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The facility is in need of a thorough scrubbing. This is just a complaint investigation so not all surfaces and preparation areas were inspected. The following non-food contact surfaces are observed soiled and in need of cleaning: 1) long carts across from the dishmachine are thickly coated with an accumulation of grease and food; 2) around the edges and pans of prep cooler tops; 3) handles of equipment and coolers (coated with grease); and 4) fryers and wok counters. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 See violation #s 23 and 7A. The long carts across from the dish machine are observed holding clean equipment, single-service articles, and utensils. Make sure that the cart is maintained clean or moved to a location where the cart and utensils will not receive so much splash from food and grease.  Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1050 Greasy waste water is observed ponding on the floor underneath the first and second sinks of the 3-compartment sink by the dishmachine. The floor is in the process of being mopped during the inspection. Make sure that leaks are maintained in order to prevent further pest problems. Repair the sink drainlines should it be warranted. All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited

Provide effective pest control.

findings.comment: 750-510d Observed one employee wash hands and turn off the faucet prior to drying. findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed facility to make their own sushi rice but has not provided a test kit to verify if sushi can be help at room temperature. Provide a pH test kit to test sushi rice. pH of sushi rice was be 4.6 or below to be allowed to store at room temperature. Until pH meter is provided, it is recommended that facility make sushi rice and store at room temperature for no longer than 4 hours once rice has been removed from 135F or above. If facility can not prove sushi rice is at a pH of 4.6 or below, do not hold below 135F longer than 4 hours. This violation should have been documented at a 3a. Until facility can prove with a pH meter that sushi rice is not potentially hazardous, it will be treated as so. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 140°F or above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - (x2) A) Fruit flies were still present at the wait station (around floor drain, shelves & wall around drink counter) and in dry storage around oil and soda syrup boxes at the wall bordering the outside of the meat walkin cooler. Work with pest control operator to find areas where flies may be breeding. Eliminate puddling water and potential food sources. Clean floor drains throughout the facility and maintain them clean. B) Small gray insects ("wood lice") were observed around motor to soda machine/below handsink at wait station where water damaged wood was observed. Bleach solution was used to clean the area/remove the insects that could be seen. The insects are more than likely living within the damaged wood. Area with water damaged wood needs to be repaired to eliminate potential hiding/breeding location for pests. Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.
**Use fly strips and UV insect traps where appropriate to help minimize number of flies**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Areas with low lying grout were noted under/behind soda machine/ice bin at wait station. A few spots with low grout in front of the soda machine/ice bin have already been repaired, and a missing piece of baseboard was replaced under the wait station handsink. Finish making repairs to the tiles at the wait station. B) Baseboard was starting to pull away at floor to cabinet junctures on both sides of wait station soda machine/ice bin. Repair/replace damaged baseboard. C) Floor drains throughout need to be cleaned. One in particular behind ice cream freezer at wait station had heavy buildup. findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 & 151 - A) Fish in sushi display cooler was at 47F-48F after being prepared this morning (temp checked ~11:15am), and cream cheese was at 39F. When checked again around 1pm fish was at 51F and cream cheese was at 48F. Products were pulled from reach-in cooler this morning, and reach-in was holding below 41F. Manager was advised to check product temperatures at 2:30pm and discard all products that are above 41F. **All products in display coolers were discarded by Manager & inspector around 4pm (internal temps were +50F). Call for service is to be made, and sushi display coolers will not be used until repairs are completed (potential issue with coils inside).**  B) Open containers of OJ and whipped topping in wait station Coke cooler were at 49F-51F. OJ and whipped topping were discarded. Other containers were moved to walkin until it could be determined unit was not failing. Thermostat was adjusted to colder setting and thermometer inside read at 40F/below. C) Fish, tofu, miso (soup base) and tempura batter in bottom of tall cook line Coke cooler had internal temperatures of 45F-51F. All products with questionable temperatures were discarded. D) Open gallon of milk in bar cooler and prepared foods (noodles, fried chicken, etc.) were not labeled with date of prep. All items were prepared or opened within the last few days and benefit of doubt was given for products to be kept for use. Properly date all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods and use or discard within 7 days. (see general comments for information on coolers and violation #3d)

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - A) Plastic container without a handle was observed down in vinegar. Plastic container was removed. B) Employee was observed using a plastic container without a handle for scooping flour from bulk container. Use of proper utensils was discussed with staff and management. C) Small black bowl was observed inside container of cooked rice. Bowl was removed from rice. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Suitable utensils, such as tongs, scoops, spoons, etc. must be used when dispensing foods.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.280 & 290 - A) Ice scoop was observed sitting on top ledge of ice machine. Scoop was placed in a pan for storage. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. B) Dipper well was not on for ice cream scoops. Dipper well was turned on by inspector. Running water must be flowing at all times when in-use utensils, such as ice cream scoops, are stored inside.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.160, 510, 512, 514 & 1120e - A) Employee on cook line was observed rinsing hands at wok faucet  and then wiping hands on a blue cloth towel. When told to wash hands at proper sink he went to 3 part sink to rinse hands. B) Employee was observed rinsing hands at prep sink. C) Used gloves (food debris present on surface) were observed sitting out at sushi bar for re-use. Hands must be properly washed at designated handsinks only using proper handwashing technique before putting on gloves, between glove changes, before handling clean equipment or food, and any time hands may be been contaminated. Common towels can not be used for wiping hands. Gloves are meant for only one task and must be discarded when torn, soiled, or when there is an interruption in service/change in tasks. Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed at length with Manager and staff. Educational handouts were once again provided including Sections 750.510 & 160 from IL Food Code.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Glass and mixing cup at bar were not properly cleaned and sanitized. Employee preparing to make drink washed and rinsed cups and then quickly dunked cups in sanitizer solution before putting ice in the mixing cup to prepare a drink. Other cups were available, so cups in question were placed off to side to go through proper ware washing process. Manual wash, rinse, sanitize were discussed with waiter. Cups, utensils, and other dishes/equipment must be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. With manual process items must stay submerged in sanitizer solution for 1 minute prior to removing and allowing items to air dry. Manual wash, rinse, sanitize handout provided. Properly train all employees on ware washing process.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - Heat sanitizing dish machine was not reaching 180F. Gauge eventually reach 180F, but temperature test strips indicated water was not reaching hot enough temperatures to properly sanitize dishes (temp test strip did not turn black). GFS was called for service. Sales representative and repair person arrived during inspection. Sales representative noted he did not see a booster heater attached to the dish machine and noted the machine was set up for chemical sanitizing at one time. Repair person ran a line for chemical sanitizer to be installed, and sales representative went to get chemical to hook up for proper sanitizing. In the meantime, the dish machine could be used for wash and rinse steps, and 3 part sink by dish machine was set up to manually chemical sanitize (50ppm chlorine) clean dishes.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was observed on cutting board at cook line prep cooler. Wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer solution. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled/not properly cleaned and sanitized: A) (see #20a) cups at bar; B) fan on top of vegetable prep cooler; C) inside dish machine (lime buildup right side); D) drip guard of ice machine (mold); & E) rice cooker with leftover fried rice from previous day of service. Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) dry storage shelves (onion storage, cooking oil & bulk spice storage, etc.); B) outside of spice containers in dry storage (garlic powder, etc.); C) bottom inside salad Coke cooler; D) inside fryers and sides of equipment on cook line; E) tracks of sliding door coolers; F) all storage tubs in dry storage area; & G) pan with old water/debris in it under motor for wait station soda machine. Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. In dry storage areas thoroughly clean all shelving and bus tubs used for general storage, especially where fruit flies were observed.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: .750.860 - A) Waiter was observed handling soup bowls by top rim and thumb was touching inside food contact surface. B) Soup spoons were stored with food surfaces and handles intermixed. C) Container of what appeared to be clean spoons were store with food surfaces extended up out of container on top of dish machine. D) Extra bowls and plates under salad/soup counter were soiled with food and general debris. Clean equipment/utensils must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects food contact surfaces from contamination. Staff must handle bowls, glasses, plates, and utensils from non-food contact surfaces (sides/bottom and handles). Cleaned/sanitized utensils must be stored with handles extended up so food contact surfaces are not being touched when utensils are being retrieved. If extra plates/bowls are not needed then place them in a different storage area where they will be protected from splash/debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text:
750.600 - A) Plastic garlic jar in small sliding door Coke cooler was being re-used for storage of eggs. B) Seaweed wrap containers were being re-used for storage of various foods (i.e. cucumber at sushi bar). Obtain and use food grade re-usable containers for food storage (i.e Ziploc). Containers that were purchased with food in them are not intended for re-use.
Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - A) Back handsink was blocked by a container upon arrival of inspector. B) Wait station handsink was used to fill a pitcher with water. C) Bar handsink was blocked by a pitcher. Items blocking handsinks were removed, and proper use of handsinks was discussed with staff and management. Handsinks must be used for handwashing only and must always be accessible at all times. Do not store anything in the basins of &/or in front of handsinks, and do not use handsinks for tasks other than handwashing.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Fruit flies were observed in dry storage around bags of onions and at wait station around floor drain below handsink. What appeared to be a fruit fly pupa (stage between maggot and adult) was observed in bottom of drain hose from wait station soda machine/ice bin. Thoroughly clean areas where flies were observed. Replace drain hose from wait station soda machine/ice bin. Eliminate puddling water from the floor around soda machine in wait station (see #36). Dispose of any onions that are not in sound condition, and thoroughly clean the shelves, all general surfaces, and the floor along walls in the dry storage area. If cleaning and general maintenance alone do not alleviate the issue then call pest control operator for service.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Back screen door had gaps along the side and the bottom where light was visible. Plastic door sweep had areas of disrepair and foam weather stripping along the side of the door was damaged/missing at the bottom half of the door. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of pests. Repair the screen door so it is tight fitting and vermin proof. A bristle door sweep may work better than plastic for the back screen door, and a more tight fitting door will eliminate a potential entry point for pests such as house flies (~2-3 observed in kitchen during inspection)

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Tiles under/around wait station soda machine/ice bin had areas with low grout. Puddling water and debris accumulation were observed in the areas with low grout. Clean and re-grout the floor tiles under/around wait station soda machine/ice bin. B) Piece of ceramic baseboard was missing below cabinet at wait station handsink. Replace missing baseboard or repair the area so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and does not accumulate debris. C) Floors were soiled under fryers, under stove, and along walls/in corners at back dry storage area. Thoroughly clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750.540a - None of the employees working at the time of the inspection had an Illinois Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification (FSSMC). Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  licensed employees that have a FSSMC to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of certified employees. **Certified manager arrived at conclusion of inspection. Discussed getting more employees in food sanitation course to be certified**

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 (x2) - A) Eggs and rice in walkin cooler were out of temperature. Rice had internal temperature of 49F and was discarded. Eggs had been out on a hibachi cart to make food for customers and were 60F-67F. Eggs were discarded. Hibachi chef and manager were advised on changing practice for eggs taken to hibachi grills (only take what is needed instead of a full container), and cooling practices/cold holding for rice and noodles were also discussed. B) Foods in Coke cooler had internal temperatures from 46F to 58F (sliced tomatoes, dressing, tofu, yum yum sauce). Foods were prepared this morning around 10:30am. All PHF was discarded at 2:30 when lunch was done. Maintain cold PHF at 41F/below at all times.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - A) Employee in kitchen was observed having bare hand contact with cooked chicken. Manager told employee to wash hands and put on gloves. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use suitable utensils and wear single use gloves when handling cooked meats and other ready to eat foods. B) Plastic containers and a bowl were observed in rice and yum yum sauce containers in walkin cooler. Containers and bowl were removed. Use proper utensils with handles for dispensing foods (i.e. scoops, spoons, measuring cup, etc.).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.510, 512, 514, & 160 - A) (x2) Employee in kitchen was asked to wash hands/put on gloves to handle cooked chicken (see #9). Employee rinsed hands at prep sink. Manager advised him on proper handwashing at a handsink. Employee washed his hands and put on gloves. Employee later rinsed the gloves after they became soiled/continued with food prep. Manager made employee change his gloves. B) Employee in dish area went from handling soiled dishes and clean dishes without washing his hands. Handwashing was discussed with the employee. Employees must properly wash their hands at designated handsinks whenever hands may have been contaminated. Gloves are meant for only one use and must be changed when soiled, torn, or when their is an interruption in service.

findings.title: Clean clothes, hair restrains
findings.comment: 750.520b -Worker in dish area was sweating profusely and was not wearing any sort of restraint to catch the sweat.  Worker had to keep wiping his head on the upper sleeve of his shirt. Hair/sweat restraint was discussed with the employee and management. Employee noted he could buy something during the break between lunch and dinner to wear for the evening shift. Employees shall use effective hair restraints such as hats, and even if employees have shaved heads they need to wear something to catch the sweat that is being produced.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Old pupa casings were noted inside soda gun holders (1 in each holder) where an adult fruit fly hatched out. Only a few fruit flies were noted in the area between the soda lines and the soda guns. Clean and sanitize the soda guns, nozzles, and especially the holders daily. Remove the holders from the drain lines, and separate the two pieces of the soda gun holders so all surfaces can be properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Floor drain at west end of bar was observed to be heavily soiled with buildup. The end of the drain line from the west end soda gun was soiled as well. Clean floor drains and the floor at the bar daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Buildup and moisture in floor drains can serve as food/water source for pests.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: NEW 750.100 - Severely dented cans were observed on #10 can rack (3 bamboo shoots & 1 pineapple juice). Old, rusty cans of soy sauce were also observed. The soy sauce in question is a product no longer used at the facility; cans of soy sauce were discarded in the trash. Cans of bamboo shoots and pineapple juice were set aside to be returned to supplier. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption. **Check products during delivers and reject questionable cans. If cans are intact but dropped/damaged by an employee, immediately open the cans and place product in a clean, properly labeled container for use. Do not keep/use cans with severe dents, rust, or other signs of damage**

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Label squeeze bottles and shakers on the cook line with the names of seasonings and liquids stored inside the containers.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: NEW 750.120 - Plastic bus tub under bar counter used to hold cans of pineapple juice and other items had standing water in it. The soda gun at the west end of the bar had a leak in it over night and is currently out of service. Manager removed items from the bus tub and cleaned the area. Manager removed wet labeled and thoroughly dried cans. Cans were then labeled, and manager was advised to use those cans immediately prior to using other cans of pineapple juice. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. **Canned and dry goods are susceptible to heat and moisture. Store canned and dry goods in clean dry locations with minimal humidity**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - General surfaces of cook line equipment need to be cleaned (sides of fryer, etc.). Clean general surfaces of cook line equipment and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - A) Shakers and squeeze bottles of seasonings and sauces on cook line were not labeled. B) Bulk storage containers were missing proper labels.  Unless the identity of a food is  unmistakable, bulk foods and any products not stored in their original packaging (i.e. cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar, flour, etc.) shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Properly label all bulk storage bins, squeeze bottles, and shakers.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 & 151 - A) Open gallon of milk in bar cooler did not have proper date mark. Milk was discarded in the trash. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be properly dated (day of prep/date opened) and consumed, sold, or discarded w/in 7 days. B) Containers of green olives & strawberry daiquiri mix (at bar) and #10 can of chili paste (on cook line) require refrigeration after opening and were sitting at room temperature +70F. All products were discarded. Maintain PHF at 41F/below or use time control (use or discard w/in 4hrs) for products that require refrigeration after opening.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Garnish tray at bar had two adult fruit flies inside touching fruit. Fruit was discarded and garnish tray was taken to dish area to be cleaned/sanitized. At all times, including while being prepared and stored, food shall be protected from potential contamination including pests. Properly store and protect foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Ice bin at bar had bottle of chocolate sauce in it, and ice bin was uncovered during the entire inspection (lid to bin was on the floor). Ice is used to make drinks in shakers and for customer drinks during dinner hours. Chocolate sauce was removed, ice was melted, and bin was cleaned. Lid to bin was ran through dish machine. Do not store anything in ice used for customer drinks, and keep ice covered between uses. B) Cans of open pineapple juice were observed in kitchen and at the bar. Juice was placed in a proper food grade containers. Do not store acidic foods in original cans after opening. Metals/metallic flavor can leach into foods making them unsafe for consumption.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - Cooked rice in walkin cooler had a bowl in it. Bowl was removed. Food handlers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods. Use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.) when dispensing foods.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.280 & 290 - A) Ice scoop at main ice machine was sitting on soiled ledge on top of machine. Holders for ice scoops at the bar were soiled with general buildup. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Properly store ice scoops. B) Multiple bulk foods had plastic containers with no handles inside, and proper scoops in bulk starch and sugar were soiled up around handles. To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used for dispensing foods. Maintain scoops clean.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.510, 512, & 1120e - A) Employee went from using bleach to working with food/equipment and did not wash his hands. B) Employee in dish area was using a common towel to wipe his hands and did not properly wash his hands (sprayed with hose) between handling soiled and clean dishes. Proper handwashing was discussed with management and employees. Common towels are prohibited; towel was placed in soiled linen storage area. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. **Educational handouts on handwashing & glove use were provided**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - A) Multiple white plates were chipped. Replace chipped plates. B) Plastic wrap was observed as lid to cherry bourbon dispenser at bar. Provide proper cover for bourbon dispenser. C) Soiled liners were observed on shelves for clean glasses at the bar. Remove all liners at the bar and throughout the entire facility. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690.- A) Coffee storage tubs at wait station were soiled and had cracked bins. Replace the soiled/damaged bins. B) Cover was broken on top of rice cooker handle. Repair or replace the rice cooker handle. C) Bottom side underneath shelves above 3 part sink next to dish machine were rusty. Clean and re-surface shelves. D) Dry storage shelves were soiled and beginning to rust. Lower shelf with rice and sugar was broken. Clean and re-surface shelves. Replace broken shelf. E) Wiping cloths, napkins, cardboard, calendar pages, and soiled foam mesh were observed lining shelves in kitchen, back counter of sushi area, speed rails at bar, and bottom inside Coke cooler at far end of cook line. Remove all wiping cloths, napkins, cardboard, calendar pages, and foam mesh throughout facility. Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth, cleanable, in good repair, and easily maintained clean.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750.820d - Compartments of 3 part sink in kitchen and drain boards of bar 3 part sink were soiled. Compartments of 3 part sinks and drain boards shall be cleaned between uses and maintained clean. Three part sink and drain boards at bar were cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Chlorine and Quat test strips were not available for checking sanitizer concentrations. Manager went and purchased test strips during the inspection. Test kits shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizers that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.
Tablets at bar = 200ppm Quat for sanitizing in 3 part sink. Chlorine = 50ppm for sanitizing in kitchen 3 part sink & 100ppm for sanitizing general surfaces and clean in place equipment.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - A) Layers of old stickers were observed on tubs used for cooked rice and noodle storage in walkin cooler. Completely remove old stickers as part of ware washing process. B) Soiled cleavers, ladels, and other utensils were observed hanging in clean utensil areas and on magnetic knife strips. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. Repeat the process as many times as necessary to remove all soil and ensure proper cleaning/sanitizing of all surfaces of utnesils and equipment.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750.800b & 820d - Hibachi chef rinsed a knife with hot water. Knife was then wiped on apron and placed back in his knife holder. Proper manual wash, rinse, sanitize of food contact surfaces was discussed. Utensils and other equipment that go through manual ware washing process were left in the 3 part sink until later when employees returned from afternoon break. Three part sink was then setup to allow for proper manual ware washing (sanitizer = 50ppm chlorine). To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment of the 3 part sink according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wiping cloth was ran under water at kitchen handsink and used to wipe ledge of vegetable prep cooler. Maintain sanitizer solution (100ppm chlorine), and store wiping cloths in solutions between uses. Use wiping cloths from sanitizer solutions for sanitizing general surfaces.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) knife rinsed/wiped on chef's apron (see #20a); B) utensils, cleavers, and ladles in clean storage areas/on magnetic knife strips (see #18); C) ice machine drip guard (mold); D) ice scoops (see #10); E) soda guns/holders (mold & fruit flies); F) slicer (food debris); G) soiled tongs hanging on oven door; H) soiled equipment inside oven; I) inside/outside of bulk food bins; J) can opener blade (food debris/metal shavings); K) inside microwaves; & L) ice cream dipper well/scoops. Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **In-use utensils (tongs, cooking utensils, etc.) must be changed out up to every 4 hours**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) walkin freezer shelves (ice); B) storage shelves throughout entire facility, especially under soiled foam mesh and other unacceptable materials used to line shelves (see #15); C) general surfaces at bar (sides of sinks, ice bins, etc.); D) outer surfaces of cooler across from dish machine; E) sliding door Coke cooler at far end of cook line (food debris in tracks, etc.); F) back counter of sushi area; & G) general surfaces of cook line equipment (fryers, sides of equipment, etc.). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Storage tubs and shelves for clean spoons, bowls, and plates were soiled with splash, food debris, and general debris. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. **Maintain storage areas & containers clean to protect items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - (x2) A) Hibachi chef used handsink to wet a wiping cloth. B) Blender pitcher was observed sitting in the basin of the bar handsink. Handsinks are to be accessible for handwashing and at all times and are to be used for handwashing only. Proper use of handsinks was discussed with staff and management.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Employee restroom was missing self closer and door was severely damaged in a few spots. Also, handsink in employee restroom was pulling away from the dry wall. Replace the door and provide a self closer. Repair or replace the handsink and dry wall. All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Fruit flies (al life stages) were observed in the soda gun holder and drain hose at the west end of the bar. Pupa that appeared near hatching into adults were observed in the hose. Old pupa casings were observed in the gun holder by the handsink on the east end of the bar. Two adult flies were in the garnish tray (touching fruit) at the ledge by the entrance to the bar. Garnish trash was taken to dish area to be cleaned/sanitized. Gun holders, guns, and nozzles were all cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Drain hose at the west end of the bar was removed and discarded in the dumpster during the inspection. Have Coke replace both drain hoses for soda guns. Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Back screen door is not tight fitting and back door was open. Screen door has gaps along the bottom and in corners where light is visible. Screen door does not completely self close. Back door was closed during the inspection. Do not leave the back door open for any length of time until screen door is properly repaired to be self closing, tight fitting, and vermin proof. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor drains throughout were in general soiled, especially under steam table, in dish area, and at west end of the bar. Drain at west end of bar was cleaned during the inspection. Maintain floor drains clean. B) Floor at bar was soiled along the wall with general buildup. Also floor to wall juncture had some gaps where grout has worn down. Floor was cleaned during the inspection. Re-grout the floor to wall juncture. C) Floor in walkin freezer was soiled with ice accumulation. Clean the floor and eliminate excess ice. Floors shall be kept clean. Floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Walls at bar were soiled with splash and general buildup. Bar staff began cleaning during the inspection. B) Ceiling and walls in walkin freezer had heavy ice/frost buildup. Clean the walkin freezer and eliminate excess ice/frost. C) Ceiling vent covers at wait station had heavy dust accumulation. Clean the vent covers. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 & 1310 - Chemical spray bottles were not labeled as to the contents in the kitchen and at the bar. Spray bottles at the bar were also hanging on the edge of the drain board next to what appeared to be clean glasses. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food and all food related items (i.e. clean glasses, etc.) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly label and store all chemicals.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of labeling on spices in the cooking area that are in plastic containers. Provide names written on containers.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed in the 2 dr refrigeration unit at the wok raw egg stored in a pan stored over the top of green pepper without a barrier in between or cover. (CORRECTED) Kitchen employee cover the container and stored on the bottom shelf of cooler.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Absence of cover for vegetables that were stored on the shelf at the walkin cooler.(CORRECTED) Provide cover or saran wrap for food containers.
750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed several clear plastic bowls stored in food product(ex. oil- cooked rice bin-orange sauce) Provide a handled scoop.
750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves..

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. The following non-food contact surfaces are observed to be soiled: 1)  handles of equipment coolers in kitchen 2) top of ice cream case in wait station. Clean and keep clean

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Knives observed to be stored between ice bin and 3 part sink.  Knives observed to be stored in soiled knife holders. Store clean utensils properly.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination. An open, partially consumed, bottle of water is observed to be stored on a shelf next to boxes of single service items.  Also hand towels are observed to be stored in restroom. Do not store single use towels in restroom. Protect single service items from contamination.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. The back screen door is not tight fitting around the bottom. Repair screen door to be tight fitting.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. The floor drains in the wait station and under the 3 part sink are soiled. Clean the floors and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Suitable storage shall be provided and used for employee belongings. A jacket is observed to be hanging on a hanger on the dry storage shelves.
